Ali al-Daher.question: On 30 _____, Ali led Daher's forces in helping the Metawalis and Druze repulse an expedition sent by the supreme army commander of Syria, Uthman Pasha al-Wakil, in the Beqaa Valley
Ali al-Daher.fact: On 30 September, Ali led Daher's forces in helping the Metawalis and Druze repulse an expedition sent by the supreme army commander of Syria, Uthman Pasha al-Wakil, in the Beqaa Valley.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He made demands of _____, which the latter rejected, leading him to declare a revolt from Safed, which he had refortified
Ali al-Daher.fact: On 30 September, Ali led Daher's forces in helping the Metawalis and Druze repulse an expedition sent by the supreme army commander of Syria, Uthman Pasha al-Wakil, in the Beqaa Valley. Ali, whose "distinctive record undoubtedly must have inspired him to attempt to succeed" Daher, especially in light of his elder brother Salibi's death the year prior, renewed his rebellion against his father.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Daher and Ahmad, who governed Tiberias and Jabal Ajlun, launched an assault on Ali in Rameh on 11 July _____
Ali al-Daher.fact: Daher and Ahmad, who governed Tiberias and Jabal Ajlun, launched an assault on Ali in Rameh on 11 July 1774.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: In the ensuing battle, Ali shot Ahmad, wounding him in the leg, then defeating Daher and forcing his father and brother to retreat to _____
Ali al-Daher.fact: In the ensuing battle, Ali shot Ahmad, wounding him in the leg, then defeating Daher and forcing his father and brother to retreat to Deir Hanna.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Daher and Ahmad, who governed Tiberias and _____, launched an assault on Ali in Rameh on 11 July 1774
Ali al-Daher.fact: Daher and Ahmad, who governed Tiberias and Jabal Ajlun, launched an assault on Ali in Rameh on 11 July 1774.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali first rebelled against _____ in March 1762 when he and his younger full brother Sa'id demanded Daher step down as a paramount sheikh or relinquish his tax farms
Ali al-Daher.fact: Beginning in the 1760s, Daher's sons began to clamor for more power within the sheikhdom and vied to position themselves as successor to their aging father, who was in his sixties by then. According to the historian Ahmad Joudah, Ali was Daher's "most competent" and "most dependable son", helping him suppress internal dissent and repulse external attacks.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali and another brother, Ahmad, backed Daher in countering a revolt by Ali's half-brother _____ al-Daher in May 1766
Ali al-Daher.fact: The brothers were supported by Daher's enemy, the governor of Damascus Uthman Pasha al-Kurji and the Metawali sheikh Nasif al-Nassar. Ali and another brother, Ahmad, backed Daher in countering a revolt by Ali's half-brother Uthman al-Daher in May 1766.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: The strife between Daher and Ali encouraged Abu al-Dhahab, who had by then replaced _____ as strongman of Egypt and was gearing up for a campaign against Daher, to ally with Ali
Ali al-Daher.fact: The strife between Daher and Ali encouraged Abu al-Dhahab, who had by then replaced Ali Bey as strongman of Egypt and was gearing up for a campaign against Daher, to ally with Ali.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: In exchange for his backing against his father, Abu al-_____ agreed to recognize him as paramount sheikh of the Zayadina
Ali al-Daher.fact: The strife between Daher and Ali encouraged Abu al-Dhahab, who had by then replaced Ali Bey as strongman of Egypt and was gearing up for a campaign against Daher, to ally with Ali. In exchange for his backing against his father, Abu al-Dhahab agreed to recognize him as paramount sheikh of the Zayadina.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Abu al-Dhahab launched his campaign in March _____, capturing Gaza and Ramla and besieging Jaffa on 3 April
Ali al-Daher.fact: Abu al-Dhahab launched his campaign in March 1775, capturing Gaza and Ramla and besieging Jaffa on 3 April.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: During the siege, Ali persuaded his brother Sa'id to discard _____'s orders to assist Jaffa's defenders
Ali al-Daher.fact: The strife between Daher and Ali encouraged Abu al-Dhahab, who had by then replaced Ali Bey as strongman of Egypt and was gearing up for a campaign against Daher, to ally with Ali. During the siege, Ali persuaded his brother Sa'id to discard Daher's orders to assist Jaffa's defenders.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Jaffa fell on 20 May and the massacre of all its men led _____'s residents to flee in panic on 23 May
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jaffa fell on 20 May and the massacre of all its men led Acre's residents to flee in panic on 23 May. He notified Abu al-Dhahab that he had driven Daher from Acre, but Abu al-Dhahab denied his demand to serve as governor and ordered his prompt withdrawal.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He notified Abu al-_____ that he had driven Daher from Acre, but Abu al-Dhahab denied his demand to serve as governor and ordered his prompt withdrawal
Ali al-Daher.fact: He notified Abu al-Dhahab that he had driven Daher from Acre, but Abu al-Dhahab denied his demand to serve as governor and ordered his prompt withdrawal. Abu al-Dhahab's forces gained control of Acre the next day and made Murad Bey governor.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Abu al-_____'s forces gained control of Acre the next day and made Murad Bey governor
Ali al-Daher.fact: He notified Abu al-Dhahab that he had driven Daher from Acre, but Abu al-Dhahab denied his demand to serve as governor and ordered his prompt withdrawal. Abu al-Dhahab's forces gained control of Acre the next day and made Murad Bey governor.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He invited Ali to meet him in _____, but Ali considered this a ruse to eliminate him and ignored the summons
Ali al-Daher.fact: He notified Abu al-Dhahab that he had driven Daher from Acre, but Abu al-Dhahab denied his demand to serve as governor and ordered his prompt withdrawal. Abu al-Dhahab's forces gained control of Acre the next day and made Murad Bey governor.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali consequently departed by 29 May, taking with him the city's cannons, munititions and provisions to _____ and Safed
Ali al-Daher.fact: Ali consequently departed by 29 May, taking with him the city's cannons, munititions and provisions to Deir Hanna and Safed.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Afterward, Abu al-_____ stormed Safed, plundering it and damaging its citadel
Ali al-Daher.fact: Abu al-Dhahab's forces gained control of Acre the next day and made Murad Bey governor. Afterward, Abu al-Dhahab stormed Safed, plundering it and damaging its citadel.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Abu al-_____ died of a sudden illness on 10 June and the next day, Daher's chief lieutenant, the commander of his Maghrebi mercenaries Ahmad Agha al-Dinkizli, moved to restore Daher's control of Acre
Ali al-Daher.fact: Abu al-Dhahab's forces gained control of Acre the next day and made Murad Bey governor. Afterward, Abu al-Dhahab stormed Safed, plundering it and damaging its citadel.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He was driven out by Ali's ally among the _____, Abdallah al-Wawi, but soon after gained control over the different Maghrebi factions
Ali al-Daher.fact: He was driven out by Ali's ally among the Maghrebis, Abdallah al-Wawi, but soon after gained control over the different Maghrebi factions.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He sent urgent notices to _____ to return to the city, otherwise it would surely be occupied by Ali; Daher reentered Acre on 12 June
Ali al-Daher.fact: Abu al-Dhahab died of a sudden illness on 10 June and the next day, Daher's chief lieutenant, the commander of his Maghrebi mercenaries Ahmad Agha al-Dinkizli, moved to restore Daher's control of Acre. He sent urgent notices to Daher to return to the city, otherwise it would surely be occupied by Ali; Daher reentered Acre on 12 June.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Initially, Ali and his brothers attempted to block supplies from the countryside reaching Acre, intending to pressure _____ into quitting the city
Ali al-Daher.fact: In conjunction with naval force, the Ottomans organized an army led by the governor of Damascus, Muhammad Pasha al-Azm, and including a force led by Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar to reassert direct government control over Acre and the Zaydani domains. Al-Jazzar was appointed governor of Sidon and made his headquarters in Acre, from where he was directed by the imperial government to eliminate the Zayadina's hold over the area and destroy their forts.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Jazzar also gained the defection of Ahmad, who was based in _____
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar also gained the defection of Ahmad, who was based in Tiberias. His territory stretched from Abu Sinan and Majd al-Krum in the west to Tiberias in the east, and besides these places also included the fortified villages of Bi'ina, Rameh, Nahf, Suhmata, Beit Jann, Sajur, Buqei'a, Julis, Yarka, Deir al-Qassi.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali, the most militarily capable and formidable of Daher's sons, remained _____'s chief obstacle to asserting power in Acre's Galilee countryside
Ali al-Daher.fact: Initially, Ali and his brothers attempted to block supplies from the countryside reaching Acre, intending to pressure Jazzar into quitting the city. It had little effect, and Jazzar soon after turned Uthman against Ali by recognizing the former as his deputy over the fortified town of Shefa-Amr and nominating him shaykh al-mashayikh of the Safed area, a nod for Uthman to oust Ali from his center of power.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: As Jazzar made preparations for war in Acre, Ali consolidated control over the _____ from his refortified Safed headquarters
Ali al-Daher.fact: Ali, the most militarily capable and formidable of Daher's sons, remained Jazzar's chief obstacle to asserting power in Acre's Galilee countryside. As Jazzar made preparations for war in Acre, Ali consolidated control over the Galilee from his refortified Safed headquarters.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He paid a large sum to _____ of Damascus to lobby the imperial government to recognize his authority over this area
Ali al-Daher.fact: He paid a large sum to Muhammad Pasha of Damascus to lobby the imperial government to recognize his authority over this area.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: In the spring of _____, Ali's horsemen launched attacks against the village's on Acre's coastal plain and almost reaching Acre's walls; they destroyed one of the two water works that supplied the city
Ali al-Daher.fact: In the spring of 1776, Ali's horsemen launched attacks against the village's on Acre's coastal plain and almost reaching Acre's walls; they destroyed one of the two water works that supplied the city.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Jazzar responded by mobilizing his troops in _____
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar responded by mobilizing his troops in Amqa. Ali gathered forces from Abu Sinan, Majd al-Krum and Deir Hanna and besieged Amqa, but a support troop from Acre dispersed his forces and relieved Jazzar.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Afterward, _____ moved on the offensive, with his forces defeating Ali's men at Abu Sinan and Jazzar personally leading a subsequent assault against Majd al-Krum
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar responded by mobilizing his troops in Amqa. Ali gathered forces from Abu Sinan, Majd al-Krum and Deir Hanna and besieged Amqa, but a support troop from Acre dispersed his forces and relieved Jazzar.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali gathered forces from _____, Majd al-Krum and Deir Hanna and besieged Amqa, but a support troop from Acre dispersed his forces and relieved Jazzar
Ali al-Daher.fact: Ali gathered forces from Abu Sinan, Majd al-Krum and Deir Hanna and besieged Amqa, but a support troop from Acre dispersed his forces and relieved Jazzar. Afterward, Jazzar moved on the offensive, with his forces defeating Ali's men at Abu Sinan and Jazzar personally leading a subsequent assault against Majd al-Krum.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: The latter was walled with a number of guard towers and garrisoned by its own population, referred to in the sources as asker-i _____
Ali al-Daher.fact: The latter was walled with a number of guard towers and garrisoned by its own population, referred to in the sources as asker-i Arab.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Jazzar subdued the fortress and executed its defenders, sending their heads to _____ as evidence of his success
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar subdued the fortress and executed its defenders, sending their heads to Constantinople as evidence of his success. These events likely preceded June, as the authorities in Constantinople had become aware of Rameh's capture by then.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: These events likely preceded June, as the authorities in _____ had become aware of Rameh's capture by then
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar subdued the fortress and executed its defenders, sending their heads to Constantinople as evidence of his success. These events likely preceded June, as the authorities in Constantinople had become aware of Rameh's capture by then.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali moved on to Rameh, where he barricaded with some 1,200 of his fighters, while _____ positioned himself in nearby Nahf, sending patrols which clashed with Ali's forces
Ali al-Daher.fact: Afterward, Jazzar moved on the offensive, with his forces defeating Ali's men at Abu Sinan and Jazzar personally leading a subsequent assault against Majd al-Krum. Jazzar subdued the fortress and executed its defenders, sending their heads to Constantinople as evidence of his success.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Viewing his position as untenable, Ali withdrew his troops from Rameh and _____, concentrating them in Deir Hanna and Safed
Ali al-Daher.fact: Viewing his position as untenable, Ali withdrew his troops from Rameh and Beit Jann, concentrating them in Deir Hanna and Safed.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Jazzar then targeted _____, which was exceptionally well-fortified, protected by a double wall, the inner with twelve towers and the outer with two
Ali al-Daher.fact: Viewing his position as untenable, Ali withdrew his troops from Rameh and Beit Jann, concentrating them in Deir Hanna and Safed. Jazzar then targeted Deir Hanna, which was exceptionally well-fortified, protected by a double wall, the inner with twelve towers and the outer with two.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali left his brother Sa'id there to stave off _____ while Ali could collect reinforcements from Safed, but Jazzar succeeded in laying siege to the village
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar then targeted Deir Hanna, which was exceptionally well-fortified, protected by a double wall, the inner with twelve towers and the outer with two. Ali left his brother Sa'id there to stave off Jazzar while Ali could collect reinforcements from Safed, but Jazzar succeeded in laying siege to the village.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Jazzar had brough in heavier weapons from Acre but these were insufficient against _____'s defenses
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar then targeted Deir Hanna, which was exceptionally well-fortified, protected by a double wall, the inner with twelve towers and the outer with two. Jazzar had brough in heavier weapons from Acre but these were insufficient against Deir Hanna's defenses.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: The tide turned in July when _____ supplied Jazzar with a heavy cannon and 200 reinforcements
Ali al-Daher.fact: The tide turned in July when Hasan Pasha supplied Jazzar with a heavy cannon and 200 reinforcements.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He sent Safed's qadi Isma'il _____ to negotiate with Jazzar, but he was turned away
Ali al-Daher.fact: He sent Safed's qadi Isma'il Effendi to negotiate with Jazzar, but he was turned away.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Jazzar proceeded with the bombardment of _____, forcing a negotiated surrender on 22 July
Ali al-Daher.fact: Jazzar proceeded with the bombardment of Deir Hanna, forcing a negotiated surrender on 22 July. Safed and Tiberias surrendered after the fall of Deir Hanna, whose fortifications were demolished.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Ali's brother Sa'id, his kethuda (chief aide) _____, his garrison commander Muhammad Abu Ghurrah, and his son Fadil were taken into Jazzar's custody
Ali al-Daher.fact: Ali's brother Sa'id, his kethuda (chief aide) Yusuf Dabbur, his garrison commander Muhammad Abu Ghurrah, and his son Fadil were taken into Jazzar's custody.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Safed and _____ surrendered after the fall of Deir Hanna, whose fortifications were demolished
Ali al-Daher.fact: Safed and Tiberias surrendered after the fall of Deir Hanna, whose fortifications were demolished. Afterward, Ali, learning of Jazzar's return to Acre, resumed operations against him, launching attempts to retake Tiberias and Deir Hanna and attacking villages around Safed.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: With his headquarters occupied and garrisoned by Jazzar's troops, Ali escaped to _____, initially taking refuge in the Shihab family's fort at Niha
Ali al-Daher.fact: With his headquarters occupied and garrisoned by Jazzar's troops, Ali escaped to Mount Lebanon, initially taking refuge in the Shihab family's fort at Niha.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Afterward, Ali, learning of _____'s return to Acre, resumed operations against him, launching attempts to retake Tiberias and Deir Hanna and attacking villages around Safed
Ali al-Daher.fact: With his headquarters occupied and garrisoned by Jazzar's troops, Ali escaped to Mount Lebanon, initially taking refuge in the Shihab family's fort at Niha. Afterward, Ali, learning of Jazzar's return to Acre, resumed operations against him, launching attempts to retake Tiberias and Deir Hanna and attacking villages around Safed.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He decisively defeated an army sent against him by _____ at Sa'sa'
Ali al-Daher.fact: With his headquarters occupied and garrisoned by Jazzar's troops, Ali escaped to Mount Lebanon, initially taking refuge in the Shihab family's fort at Niha. Afterward, Ali, learning of Jazzar's return to Acre, resumed operations against him, launching attempts to retake Tiberias and Deir Hanna and attacking villages around Safed.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: He had the advantage of mobility and a friendly population in the _____'s villages, which sustained his revolt
Ali al-Daher.fact: He had the advantage of mobility and a friendly population in the Galilee's villages, which sustained his revolt. In the historian Amnon Cohen's words, "With this troublesome thorn [Ali] removed from his side, Jezzār could now breathe far more easily." Ali's assassination marked the end of the Zayadina's power in the Galilee, giving Jazzar full control of the area and allowing him to move against the Metawali chiefs in Jabal Amil.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: In mid-November _____, an officer serving Muhammad Pasha of Damascus who had gained entry into Ali's camp struck and killed Ali, sending his head to Constantinople
Ali al-Daher.fact: In mid-November 1776, an officer serving Muhammad Pasha of Damascus who had gained entry into Ali's camp struck and killed Ali, sending his head to Constantinople.

Ali al-Daher.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Daher.question: Abu al-_____ launched his campaign in March 1775, capturing Gaza and Ramla and besieging Jaffa on 3 April
Ali al-Daher.fact: The strife between Daher and Ali encouraged Abu al-Dhahab, who had by then replaced Ali Bey as strongman of Egypt and was gearing up for a campaign against Daher, to ally with Ali. In exchange for his backing against his father, Abu al-Dhahab agreed to recognize him as paramount sheikh of the Zayadina.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: The _____ was Islamic scholar (born 1930).
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Ali al-Husayni al-Sistani (Arabic: علي الحسيني السيستاني; born 4 August 1930) is an Islamic scholar and the dean of the Hawza in Najaf, Iraq. A Grand Ayatollah, Sistani is considered one of the leading religious leaders of Twelver Shia Muslims.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Ali al-Husayni al-Sistani (Arabic: علي الحسيني السيستاني; born 4 August _____) is an Islamic scholar and the dean of the Hawza in Najaf, Iraq
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Ali al-Husayni al-Sistani (Arabic: علي الحسيني السيستاني; born 4 August 1930) is an Islamic scholar and the dean of the Hawza in Najaf, Iraq.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: A _____, Sistani is considered one of the leading religious leaders of Twelver Shia Muslims
Ali al-Sistani.fact: A Grand Ayatollah, Sistani is considered one of the leading religious leaders of Twelver Shia Muslims.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: After the invasion of Iraq and the subsequent overthrow of the authoritarian _____ regime, Sistani advocated for democratization instead of the system of Wilayat al-Faqih
Ali al-Sistani.fact: After the invasion of Iraq and the subsequent overthrow of the authoritarian Baathist regime, Sistani advocated for democratization instead of the system of Wilayat al-Faqih.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: He has likewise endorsed rule of law, _____ nationalism, non-sectarianism and popular sovereignty
Ali al-Sistani.fact: He has likewise endorsed rule of law, Iraqi nationalism, non-sectarianism and popular sovereignty. He has been a vocal critic of foreign interference in Iraqi affairs and has warned foreign actors against imposing their will on the Iraqi people.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: He has been a vocal critic of foreign interference in _____ affairs and has warned foreign actors against imposing their will on the Iraqi people
Ali al-Sistani.fact: He has likewise endorsed rule of law, Iraqi nationalism, non-sectarianism and popular sovereignty. He has been a vocal critic of foreign interference in Iraqi affairs and has warned foreign actors against imposing their will on the Iraqi people.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Born in _____, Iran to a Sayyid family, Sistani studied in Qom under Hossein Borujerdi and later in Najaf under Abu al-Qasim al-Khu'i
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Born in Mashhad, Iran to a Sayyid family, Sistani studied in Qom under Hossein Borujerdi and later in Najaf under Abu al-Qasim al-Khu'i.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: An Usuli, Sistani rose to the rank of mujtahid in _____ and succeeded Abd al-A'la al-Sabziwari as Grand Ayatollah
Ali al-Sistani.fact: An Usuli, Sistani rose to the rank of mujtahid in 1960 and succeeded Abd al-A'la al-Sabziwari as Grand Ayatollah.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Sistani rose to the rank of mujtahid in _____ at thirty-one
Ali al-Sistani.fact: An Usuli, Sistani rose to the rank of mujtahid in 1960 and succeeded Abd al-A'la al-Sabziwari as Grand Ayatollah.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Sistani was included in top positions of The Muslim 500: The World's Most Influential Muslims from _____ to 2024 and named one of the 100 most influential people in the world by Time magazine in 2004
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Sistani was included in top positions of The Muslim 500: The World's Most Influential Muslims from 2004 to 2024 and named one of the 100 most influential people in the world by Time magazine in 2004 and 2005.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: His father was _____-Baqir al-Sistani and his mother was the daughter of Ridha al-Mehrebani al-Sarabi
Ali al-Sistani.fact: His father was Mohammad-Baqir al-Sistani and his mother was the daughter of Ridha al-Mehrebani al-Sarabi.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Despite the family surname being "Sistani", the family was not of _____ origin but of Arab Sayyid origin
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Despite the family surname being "Sistani", the family was not of Sistani Persian origin but of Arab Sayyid origin.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: The surname derived from his great grandfather, _____ al-Husayni, who was appointed as Sheikh al-Islam in Sistan by the last Safavid Shah Hossein and established his residence there
Ali al-Sistani.fact: The surname derived from his great grandfather, Muhammad al-Husayni, who was appointed as Sheikh al-Islam in Sistan by the last Safavid Shah Hossein and set up his residence there.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: The delegation also mentioned that _____ frequently mentioned the Arab nation and criticized the Velayat-e-Faqih system of Iran
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Despite the family surname being "Sistani", the family was not of Sistani Persian origin but of Arab Sayyid origin. After the 2003 invasion of Iraq, a Sunni Arab tribal delegation visited Sistani, and noted that despite speaking imperfect Standard Arabic with a heavy Persian accent, Sistani made it clear that he was an Arab and that the influence of his Iranian upbringing did not change the fact that he was a Sayyid.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Sistani began his religious education as a child, first in _____ in his father's hawza, and continuing later in Qom
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Sistani began his religious education as a child, first in Mashhad in his father's hawza, and continuing later in Qom.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Later in _____, Sistani traveled to Iraq to study in Najaf under Grand Ayatollah Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Later in 1951, Sistani traveled to Iraq to study in Najaf under Grand Ayatollah Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: However, when he died in _____, Sistani ascended to the rank of Grand Ayatollah through formal peer recognition of his scholarship
Ali al-Sistani.fact: However, when he died in 1993, Sistani ascended to the rank of Grand Ayatollah through formal peer recognition of his scholarship.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: His role as successor to _____ was symbolically cemented when he led funeral prayers for Khoei, and he also inherited most of Khoei's network and following
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Later in 1951, Sistani traveled to Iraq to study in Najaf under Grand Ayatollah Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei. His role as successor to Khoei was symbolically cemented when he led funeral prayers for Khoei, and he also inherited most of Khoei's network and following.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Sistani's mosque was forcefully shut down in _____ and did not reopen until the 2003 American-led invasion of Iraq
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Sistani's mosque was forcefully shut down in 1994 and did not reopen until the 2003 American-led invasion of Iraq.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Later, _____ called for a democratic vote of the people to form a transitional government
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Sistani's mosque was forcefully shut down in 1994 and did not reopen until the 2003 American-led invasion of Iraq. Shortly after the American invasion began, Sistani issued a fatwa advising Shia clergy to become engaged in politics to better guide the Iraqi people toward "clearer decisions" and to fight "media propaganda." As the summer of 2003 approached, Sistani and his followers began petitioning the occupying forces for a constitutional convention.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: Observers described the move as being a path leading directly to Shia political dominance over Iraq's government, as _____ make up approximately 65% of the total Iraqi population
Ali al-Sistani.fact: Observers described the move as being a path leading directly to Shia political dominance over Iraq's government, as Shia Muslims make up approximately 65% of the total Iraqi population.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: In early August _____, Sistani experienced serious health complications related to a previously diagnosed heart condition
Ali al-Sistani.fact: In early August 2004, Sistani experienced serious health complications related to a previously diagnosed heart condition.

Ali al-Sistani.subject: International Relations
Ali al-Sistani.question: He traveled to _____ to receive medical treatment
Ali al-Sistani.fact: He traveled to London to receive medical treatment.
